event.canonical_title: Iran Claims Attacks on US Bases in Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait Amid Escalating Conflict
event.summary: Iran's military announced it targeted US military bases in Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait in retaliation for recent US strikes on Iran. The Iranian Revolutionary Guards reportedly aimed at a data center in Bahrain linked to Amazon. This escalation follows a vow from the US for 'major military punishment' against Tehran and its allies.

event_overview.title: About Iran Conflict
event_overview.subject: Iran Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Iran Conflict refers here to the 2026 direct military confrontation between the United States and Iran, which has expanded beyond Iranian territory to include attacks and claimed attacks on U.S. forces, partner states and maritime activity in the Middle East. The confrontation has centered in part on control and security of the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran’s reported retaliatory operations have involved missiles and drones directed at regional sites hosting U.S. personnel.

facts.label: Start of the direct conflict
facts.value: Reporting describes U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28, 2026, as the start of the present direct war; it is distinct from the longer-running U.S.-Iran rivalry and regional proxy conflicts.

facts.label: Ceasefire and renewed fighting
facts.value: The United States and Iran reached an interim arrangement or ceasefire in mid-June 2026, but reporting says the truce subsequently broke down amid a confrontation over the Strait of Hormuz and renewed U.S. and Iranian attacks.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The conflict’s military and economic effects extend across Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and neighboring states that host U.S. facilities, including Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan; reports of individual strikes and damage may be contested or unverified.

facts.label: Why Bahrain and Kuwait matter
facts.value: Bahrain hosts U.S. Naval Support Activity Bahrain and the U.S. Fifth Fleet/NAVCENT presence, while Camp Arifjan in Kuwait supports Army prepositioned stocks and theater sustainment for U.S. Central Command operations.

facts.label: Maritime dimension
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz is a central theater because it is a strategic shipping chokepoint; the U.S. Fifth Fleet’s area of responsibility includes the Arabian Gulf and the strait, alongside other regional waterways.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline follows selected 2026 escalations involving U.S.-Iran military and maritime actions, including reported attacks affecting U.S. regional facilities, rather than documenting every diplomatic, proxy, domestic or historical aspect of U.S.-Iran relations.
